senses.gloss:
mlecchas
(‘those who speak in an uncultured way’)
------------------------------------------
The word ‘mleccha’ has often been used in the epics and the पुराणस् to describe the non-Āryan tribes who perhaps came from outside the country. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (3.2.1.23 and 24) declares that those who speak an incorrect and corrupt dialect are असुरस् and म्लेच्छस्. The Gautama-dharmasūtras (9.17) prohibits a person from speaking with म्लेच्छस् as also impure and irreligious persons. People of countries beyond the आर्यावर्त, where the varṇāśrama system did not exist, had been dubbed as म्लेच्छस्.
The Mahābhārata has some interesting details about the म्लेच्छस्: 1. They were produced from the tail of the celestial cow Nandinī of वसिष्ठ and drove away the army of विश्वामित्र. 2. They were living in the coastal regions and their king was अङ्ग. 3. अङ्ग was killed by भीम in the कुरुक्षेत्र war. 4. The wealth that was left over in the yāgaśālā (sacrificial shed) of युधिष्ठिर (after the अश्वमेध sacrifice) was taken away by the म्लेच्छस्. 5. कल्कि, the future इन्चर्नतिओन् of विष्णु will destroy the म्लेच्छस् who will be found everywhere in the world.
In the later period, by the time of the Bhaviṣyapurāṇa (A. D. 900), the म्लेच्छस् seem to have been absorbed as a caste at the lowest rung of the social ladder. They have been described as the eaters of cow’s flesh and selling their children for financial benefits. But they could worship the clay images of the देवी and other gods.
